claims.claim: The paper reports statistically significant articulatory differences among several perceptually salient /r/ and /s/ error subtypes and correct targets in American English.
claims.limitations: The study is limited to selected American-English child error types and an inversion model; clinical interpretability is demonstrated for these comparisons, not established for all disorders or speakers. No independent reproduction was performed.

claims.claim: On Libri-3Mix-derived data covering eleven clean, noisy, reverberant, mixed, and combined conditions, FATE reports comparable enhancement quality while reducing unnecessary processing and avoiding overprocessing clean inputs.
claims.limitations: The degradations are simulated and drawn from specified mixtures, noises, and rooms; real rooms, analyzer errors, and out-of-distribution combinations are not established. The reported score is author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

claims.claim: The paper reports WER of 7.9% on LibriMix and 32.9% on AMI SDM at biasing size 1,000, outperforming compared contextual-biasing approaches in its reported settings.
claims.limitations: FIFO serialization imposes an ordering convention; the bias list and first-pass filter supply information that may not exist in every deployment. WER does not separately reveal speaker attribution, rare-word recall, or hallucination cost, and results were not independently reproduced.

claims.claim: The reported benchmark finds that all three tested systems still struggle with user interruptions, frequent disruptions, and noisy conditions; the paper states that data and code will be released.
claims.limitations: The conversations and interruptions are simulated/generated, and benchmark metrics are proxies for human experience. Release claims are not equivalent to artifact execution here; no independent reproduction or user study was performed.

claims.claim: The paper reports significantly improved speaker-similarity scores while maintaining high speech quality in diffusion-based voice-conversion experiments.
claims.limitations: Time reversal may remove more or less information depending on language and model; the experiments do not establish universal speaker/language disentanglement or human identity judgments across populations. No independent reproduction was performed.

claims.claim: The paper reports min a-DCF improving from 0.329 to 0.233 for the A26 attack with parameter sharing and a 14.09% gain for AMR-compressed signals in the tested setup.
claims.limitations: Benefits are attack- and codec-specific; the ASVspoof 5 protocols do not exhaust future generators or deployment channels. min a-DCF is a system-level proxy, not proof of safe authentication, and no independent reproduction was performed.

claims.claim: The authors report improved ASR on monolingual and code-switched tests, with the largest gains for BM-EN followed by TA-EN and ZH-BM.
claims.limitations: Synthetic phrase mixing is an approximation to spontaneous switching, and the three language pairs do not represent all multilingual communities. WER does not measure whether switches are socially or linguistically natural, and no independent reproduction was performed.

claims.claim: The paper reports a 55% relative EER reduction on In-the-Wild to 1.7% absolute EER and a 63% reduction on AI4T after the data-centric interventions.
claims.limitations: The new dataset and curation choices define the tested notion of real-world variation; future generators and channels may differ. EER is not a guarantee of safe moderation or authentication, and no independent reproduction was performed.
